requirements.original: _SuperSet is denoted by the keyword superset.
requirements.canonical: The SuperSet matching mechanism IS denoted by the keyword `superset`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- _SuperSet is denoted by the keyword superset.

requirements.original: SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values_ contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and may contain more.
requirements.canonical: SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and possibly more.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values_ contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and may contain more.

requirements.original: The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to the elements of the set of values where each SuperSet element matches the element of set of values it is mapped to.
requirements.canonical: SuperSet SHALL produce a successful match only if there exists a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to elements of the set of values such that each SuperSet element matches the element it is mapped to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to the elements of the set of values where each SuperSet element matches the element of set of values it is mapped to.

requirements.original: The SuperSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.
requirements.canonical: A SuperSet MAY contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction, and matching mechanisms subject to the restrictions of clause B.1.2.6.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- The SuperSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.

requirements.original: However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the _SuperSet itself._
requirements.canonical: A length matching attribute MAY be attached to a SuperSet as a whole.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the _SuperSet itself._

requirements.original: NOTE: The SuperSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values, i.e. the set of values contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet template in order to produce a successful match.
requirements.canonical: A set of values matched by a SuperSet contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet (implicit length restriction).
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- NOTE: The SuperSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values, i.e. the set of values contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet template in order to produce a successful match.

requirements.original: Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SuperSets using an all from clause._
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause MAY be used in a SuperSet to add all elements of a record of or set of template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SuperSets using an all from clause._

requirements.original: a) SuperSet is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of set of types.
requirements.canonical: SuperSet SHALL be used only on values of set of types.

ambiguity.issue: SuperSet is called an 'operation for matching' although it is a matching mechanism.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- a) SuperSet is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of set of types.

requirements.original: b) Individual members of the SuperSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.
requirements.canonical: Each individual member of a SuperSet's argument SHALL be of the member type of the associated set of type.

ambiguity.issue: 'type replicated by the set of' is used for the member type of the set of type.

improper_terms.used: type replicated by the set of
improper_terms.proper: member type of the set of type

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- b) Individual members of the SuperSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.

requirements.original: c) The member type of the set of associated with the SuperSet template and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
requirements.canonical: The member type of the set of type associated with a SuperSet and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that SuperSet SHALL be compatible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- c) The member type of the set of associated with the SuperSet template and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.

requirements.original: d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.

requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except those prohibited by restriction e) of clause B.1.2.6.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.original: e) The individual members of the SuperSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SuperSet's argument and an element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL NOT be `omit`, SuperSet, SubSet, a length restriction or `ifpresent`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- e) The individual members of the SuperSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

requirements.original: In addition, the individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SuperSet's argument SHALL NOT resolve to AnyValueOrNone.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- In addition, the individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone

requirements.original: individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.

requirements.original: f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute shall not be less than the number of the elements in the SuperSet.
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is attached to a SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute SHALL NOT be less than the number of elements in the SuperSet.
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute shall not be less than the number of the elements in the SuperSet.

requirements.original: g) Templates in SuperSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: A template in a SuperSet's argument SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.6 -- g) Templates in SuperSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: _SubSet is denoted by the keyword subset.
requirements.canonical: The SubSet matching mechanism IS denoted by the keyword `subset`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- _SubSet is denoted by the keyword subset.

requirements.original: SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains_ only elements defined within the SubSet, and may contain less.
requirements.canonical: SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains only elements defined within the SubSet, and possibly fewer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains_ only elements defined within the SubSet, and may contain less.

requirements.original: The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements where each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.
requirements.canonical: SubSet SHALL produce a successful match only if there exists a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements such that each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements where each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.

requirements.original: The SubSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.
requirements.canonical: A SubSet MAY contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction, and matching mechanisms subject to the restrictions of clause B.1.2.7.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- The SubSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.

requirements.original: However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the SubSet itself.
requirements.canonical: A length matching attribute MAY be attached to a SubSet as a whole.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the SubSet itself.

requirements.original: The SubSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values: the set of values shall contain at most as many elements as the SubSet template in order to produce a successful match.
requirements.canonical: A set of values SHALL contain at most as many elements as the SubSet in order to be matched by the SubSet (implicit length restriction).
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- The SubSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values: the set of values shall contain at most as many elements as the SubSet template in order to produce a successful match.

requirements.original: Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SubSets using an all from clause._
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause MAY be used in a SubSet to add all elements of a record of or set of template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SubSets using an all from clause._

requirements.original: a) SubSet is an operation for matching that can be used only on values of set of types.
requirements.canonical: SubSet SHALL be used only on values of set of types.

ambiguity.issue: SubSet is called an 'operation for matching' although it is a matching mechanism; 'can be used only' is normalized to SHALL.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- a) SubSet is an operation for matching that can be used only on values of set of types.

requirements.original: b) Individual members of the SubSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.
requirements.canonical: Each individual member of a SubSet's argument SHALL be of the member type of the associated set of type.

ambiguity.issue: 'type replicated by the set of' is used for the member type of the set of type.

improper_terms.used: type replicated by the set of
improper_terms.proper: member type of the set of type

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- b) Individual members of the SubSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.

requirements.original: c) The member type of the set of type associated with the SubSet and the member type of the template in the allfrom clause shall be compatible.
requirements.canonical: The member type of the set of type associated with a SubSet and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that SubSet SHALL be compatible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- c) The member type of the set of type associated with the SubSet and the member type of the template in the allfrom clause shall be compatible.

requirements.original: d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a matching mechanism or combined template.
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'a matching mechanism or combined template', whereas the corresponding restrictions for template list, complement and SuperSet say 'a specific value or combined template', and EXAMPLE 2 of B.1.2.1/B.1.2.2 shows that an all from template resolving into a matching mechanism as a whole is an error. The 'specific value' reading is chosen as the likely intent.
readings: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a matching mechanism or a combined template.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a matching mechanism or combined template.

requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except those prohibited by restriction e) of clause B.1.2.7.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.original: e) The individual members of the SubSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument and an element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT be `omit`, SuperSet, SubSet, a length restriction or `ifpresent`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- e) The individual members of the SubSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

requirements.original: In addition, individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument SHALL NOT resolve to AnyValueOrNone.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- In addition, individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone

requirements.original: individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.

requirements.original: f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute shall not exceed the number of the elements in the SubSet.
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is attached to a SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute SHALL NOT exceed the number of elements in the SubSet.
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute shall not exceed the number of the elements in the SubSet.

requirements.original: g) Templates in SubSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: A template in a SubSet's argument SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.7 -- g) Templates in SubSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: If used as a matching mechanism, it matches an optional field or a map key if and only if it is absent.
requirements.canonical: When used as a matching mechanism, `omit` matches an optional field or a map key if, and only if, the field or key is absent.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.8 -- If used as a matching mechanism, it matches an optional field or a map key if and only if it is absent.

requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.canonical: `omit` MAY be assigned to a template of any type as a whole, to an optional field of a set or record template, or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.8 -- a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.canonical: `omit` SHALL NOT be assigned to a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.8 -- a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.original: b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.
requirements.canonical: At the time of matching during a receiving operation, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a template that is `omit` as a whole (allowed by restriction a) may be used directly in a receiving operation, and whether a violation is a compile-time or a runtime error. The reading that a top-level `omit` is not allowed in a receiving operation is chosen.
readings: A template that is `omit` as a whole SHALL NOT be used as the top-level template of a receiving operation.
A template that is `omit` as a whole MAY be used in a receiving operation only when referenced from an optional field or map value; otherwise the matching causes a runtime error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.8 -- b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.

requirements.original: The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol IS composed of the `decmatch` keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

requirements.original: A template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and if the decoded instance can be successfully matched by the decoding target.
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses `decmatch` matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and the decoded instance is successfully matched by the decoding target.
requirements.condition: the template field uses the MatchDecodedContent matching symbol
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- A template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and if the decoded instance can be successfully matched by the decoding target.

requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` MAY specify one of the UCS encoding formats.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).
requirements.canonical: If the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is present, the specified encoding format SHALL be used for the decoding trial.
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or to the type of the decoding target.
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be assigned' in a Restrictions list; chose the restrictive reading (only these types).
readings: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol MAY be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types (other types not explicitly excluded).

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- a) It can be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

requirements.original: b) The decoding target can be a template of any data type.
requirements.canonical: The decoding target of `decmatch` MAY be a template of any data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- b) The decoding target can be a template of any data type.

requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.

ambiguity.issue: The source text is garbled ('fields of r universal charstring types'), and restriction d) implies an encoding format also applies to charstring fields; chose universal charstring only, as literally written.
readings: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.
The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of charstring or universal charstring type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be of charstring type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` predefined function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter value is not one of the strings allowed for decvalue_unichar

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time or a runtime error; chose 'an error' generically (compile-time if the value is known statically, otherwise runtime).
readings: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a compile-time error.
An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a runtime error when matching is performed.

requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- Any other value shall cause an error.

requirements.original: d) If the template field is of charstring type or is of universal charstring type and the encoding format is missing, the default value "UTF-8" shall be used.
requirements.canonical: If the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is missing, the encoding format "UTF-8" SHALL be used.
requirements.condition: the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter is missing
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- d) If the template field is of charstring type or is of universal charstring type and the encoding format is missing, the default value "UTF-8" shall be used.

requirements.original: Decoding is successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string (i.e. the whole encoded value has been successfully decoded).
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding IS successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string after decoding.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- Decoding is successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string (i.e. the whole encoded value has been successfully decoded).

requirements.original: The matching mechanism will generate an unsuccessful match if decoding hasn't succeeded.
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching mechanism produces an unsuccessful match if decoding has not succeeded.
requirements.header: // @requirement: B.1.2.9 -- The matching mechanism will generate an unsuccessful match if decoding hasn't succeeded.
